name: V60 Pour-Over
description: A clean, bright cup brewed by hand-pouring water over a cone of coffee in stages.

steps.text: Heat water to 92–96 °C. Rinse the paper filter with hot water and throw the rinse water away.
Grind 15 g of coffee medium-fine, about like table salt, and level the bed.
Bloom: pour about 45 g of water to wet all the grounds and wait while it bubbles.
Pour to 100 g in slow circles, avoiding the paper edges. Wait until the 1:00 mark.
Pour to 150 g, then at 1:30 pour the rest up to 250 g.
Give the dripper a gentle swirl and let it drain. Aim to finish around 3:00–3:30.

tips: Light roasts like the hotter end of the range; dark roasts the cooler end.
Drains too slowly? Grind coarser. Too fast and sour? Grind finer.

sources.name: Origin Coffee — V60 brew guide
Coffee Hero — V60 golden ratio 1:16
Heirloom Coffee Roasters — Pour-over guide

name: Chemex
description: An hourglass pour-over with a thick paper filter for an ultra-clean, tea-like cup to share.

steps.text: Fold the filter so the triple-layered side faces the spout. Rinse it with hot water, then pour the water out.
Grind the coffee medium-coarse, like kosher salt, and add it to the filter.
Bloom: pour about 90 g of water to saturate the grounds.
Pour in slow spirals, keeping the slurry level steady, until you reach 630 g total.
Let it drain completely. The whole brew should take about 4–5 minutes.
Lift out the filter, swirl the carafe and pour.

tips: The thick filter needs a coarser grind than a V60.

sources.name: Stumptown — Chemex brew guide
Equator Coffees — Chemex recipe

name: French Press
description: Full-bodied immersion coffee. Steep, press, pour: about as forgiving as brewing gets.

steps.text: Boil water and let it rest for about 30 seconds, down to roughly 93–96 °C.
Add 30 g of coarsely ground coffee (like sea salt) to the press.
Pour in all the water, making sure every ground is wet. Put the lid on without pressing.
Break the crust with a spoon and skim off the floating foam and grounds.
Press the plunger down slowly and gently.
Pour it all out straight away. Coffee left on the grounds turns bitter.

sources.name: Bean Box — How to use a French press
Coffee Gear Hub — French press brew guide

name: AeroPress (Standard)
description: A quick plunger brew that makes a clean, rich cup in about two minutes.

steps.text: Put a paper filter in the cap, rinse it, and screw it on. Stand the AeroPress on a sturdy mug.
Add 15 g of medium-fine coffee.
Pour in 210 g of water and stir a few times.
Insert the plunger and press down gently and steadily for about 30 seconds, stopping at the hiss.

tips: Top up with hot water if you want a longer, americano-style cup.

sources.name: Wikipedia — AeroPress
Coffee Brew Guides — AeroPress guide

name: AeroPress (Inverted)
description: Brew upside-down so nothing drips early: a fuller-bodied immersion cup.

steps.text: Push the plunger in about 1 cm and stand the AeroPress upside down on the plunger.
Add 17 g of medium grind coffee, then pour about 50 g of water to bloom.
Add the rest of the water (to 250 g) and stir gently.
Screw on the cap with a rinsed filter, put your mug upside down on top, and carefully flip everything over.
Press slowly for about 30 seconds.

tips: Flip carefully! Keep one hand on the chamber and one on the mug.

sources.name: Perfect Daily Grind — The inverted AeroPress method
Methodical Coffee — AeroPress inverted

name: Moka Pot
description: Italy's stovetop brewer: strong, concentrated coffee that's the closest thing to espresso without a machine.

steps.text: Fill the bottom chamber with hot (not boiling) water up to just below the safety valve.
Fill the basket with medium-fine coffee and level it off. Don't tamp.
Screw the pot together, using a towel because the base is hot, and set it on medium-low heat with the lid open.
When coffee starts to flow, watch closely. Once it turns pale and starts to sputter, take it off the heat.
Run the base under cold water to stop extraction, then pour.

tips: Starting with hot water shortens the time on the stove and avoids a burnt taste.

sources.name: Blue Bottle — Moka pot brew guide
Stumptown — How to brew in a moka pot

name: Better Drip Coffee
description: Your auto-drip machine, dialled in with a proper ratio and fresh water.

steps.text: Fill the reservoir with fresh, cold filtered water.
Rinse the paper filter, then add about 60 g (roughly 8 level tbsp) of medium ground coffee for a litre of water.
Start the brew. When it finishes, give the carafe a swirl so the strength is even.
Pour into a thermos or turn off the hot plate so it doesn't stew.

sources.name: Coffee Gear Hub — Coffee ratio chart
Coffee Hero — The 1:16 golden ratio

name: Cold Brew Concentrate
description: Coffee steeped overnight in cold water. Smooth, low-acid, and ready in the fridge all week.

steps.text: Grind the coffee very coarse, coarser than for a French press.
Stir the grounds and cold water together in a jar until everything is wet.
Cover and steep 12–18 hours in the fridge (or 10–12 at room temperature).
Strain through a fine sieve lined with a paper filter or cloth.
To serve, dilute about 1:1 to 1:2 with water or milk over ice.

tips: Keeps about 2 weeks in a sealed jar in the fridge.
A French press makes straining easy: steep in it, then press.

sources.name: JayArr Coffee — Cold brew concentrate guide
Barista At Home — Cold brew ratio

name: Japanese Iced Coffee
description: Pour-over brewed hot straight onto ice. It flash-chills and keeps the bright, fruity flavours.

steps.text: Weigh 200 g of ice into your carafe and set the dripper on top.
Grind 30 g of coffee a little finer than for a hot pour-over.
Bloom with about 60 g of hot water.
Pour the rest of the hot water in slow circles until you've added 300 g total.
Once it drains, swirl until most of the ice melts, then pour over fresh ice.

tips: The ice is part of the brew water, so the hot portion is brewed extra strong.

sources.name: Doppio — James Hoffmann's iced filter coffee
Gear Patrol — Japanese-style iced coffee

name: Cowboy Coffee
description: Campfire coffee: boil grounds right in the pot, then settle them with a splash of cold water.

steps.text: Heat the water in a saucepan until it's just about to boil, then take it off the heat.
Stir in the coarse grounds and let them steep.
Stir again and steep a couple more minutes.
Sprinkle about 60 ml of cold water over the surface. It sinks and pulls the grounds down with it.
Pour slowly into mugs, leaving the last bit and the sludge in the pot.

sources.name: Trade Coffee — How to make cowboy coffee
Driftaway Coffee — How do you make cowboy coffee?
